1	# EXCLURAD
2	
3	Fortran code for calculation of QED radiative corrections to exclusive
4	electroproduction on the nucleon. The current repository contains two
5	configurations:
6	
7	- **Pion electroproduction** (original 2002 code): corrections to the
8	  unpolarized coincidence cross section and beam spin asymmetry (fifth
9	  structure function) for ep → e'nπ⁺.
10	- **η-meson electroproduction** (2025 extension): adapted for ep → e'pη
11	  using updated EtaMAID-2023 hadronic model tables and CLAS12 kinematics.
12	
13	Distinctive features of the underlying formalism:
14	- Covariant infrared divergence cancellation (Bardin–Shumeiko method),
15	  giving results independent of the soft/hard photon splitting parameter.
16	- Exact integration over the bremsstrahlung photon phase space — no
17	  peaking approximation.
18	
19	The code is extendable to any exclusive two-body electroproduction process,
20	e.g. p(e,e'K)Λ, d(e,e'p)n, ³He(e,e'p)d.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## References
25	
26	Original pion code:
27	
28	> A. Afanasev, I. Akushevich, V. Burkert, K. Joo,  
29	> *QED Radiative Corrections in Processes of Exclusive Pion Electroproduction*,  
30	> Phys. Rev. D **66**, 074004 (2002). [hep-ph/0208183](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0208183)
31	
32	η-meson extension:
33	
34	> I. Illari, A. Afanasev, W.J. Briscoe, V.L. Kashevarov, A. Schmidt, I. Strakovsky,  
35	> *Amplitude-Based Analysis of QED Radiative Corrections to Electroproduction of η-Mesons on Protons*,  
36	> [arXiv:2604.22943](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22943),
37	> [accepted in Phys. Rev. D](https://journals.aps.org/prd/accepted/10.1103/78q1-72dn) (2026).
38	
39	Code and data archived at [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18970109](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18970109).
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Interactive RC Explorer
44	
45	A browser-based visualisation of the η-channel radiative correction output
46	(δ = σ_obs/σ₀ and A_RC/A_Born) is available at:
47	
48	**<https://izzyillari.github.io/exclurad/>**
49	
50	The dataset was computed with the η-channel configuration described below
51	(vcut = 0.166 GeV², beam energy 6.53 GeV, full O(α) corrections) and now
52	covers the full production grid: W = 1.487–2.211 GeV, Q² = 0.3–5.0 GeV²,
53	cos θ* = ±0.9, full φ* range — about 1.9 million kinematic points.

60	
61	```
62	exclurad/
63	├── exclurad.F          # Main Fortran source (η-modified)
64	├── fint.F              # CERNLIB-free numerical integration
65	├── mpintp.inc          # Mass/channel constants (η configuration)

77	│   ├── README.md
78	│   ├── rcgrid_inputgen.py       # 4D kinematic grid generator
79	│   ├── run_exclurad_grid.sh     # Verbose sequential runner

82	    ├── README.md

84	    ├── exclurad_run_chunk.sbatch       # Chunk array (pre-generated grid)

86	    └── exclu_vcut_scan.sbatch          # ν_cut scan at fixed kinematics

92

103	# GNU make
104	make
105	
106	# or SCons (original build system)

110	The executable is written to `build/exclurad.exe`.

116	
117	```bash
118	./build/exclurad.exe < input.dat
119	```
120	
121	Outputs are written to the current directory: `all.dat`, `allu.dat`,
122	`radasm.dat`, `radcor.dat`, `radsigmi.dat`, `radsigpl.dat`, `radtot.dat`.
123	
124	---

126	## Input file format
127	
128	```
129	3       !  1: AO  2: maid98  3: maid2000
130	0       !  0: Full, 1: Factorizable and Leading log
131	6.53    !  bmom - lepton momentum [GeV]
132	0.0     !  tmom - momentum per nucleon
133	1       !  lepton - 1 electron, 2 muon
134	1       !  ivec  - detected hadron (1) p, (2) pi+
135	0.166   !  vcut  - cut on inelasticity [GeV²] (0 = no cut)
136	
137	10 ! no. of points
138	<W values>        ! W [GeV]
139	<Q² values>       ! Q² [GeV²]
140	<cos(θ*) values>  ! Cos(Theta*)
141	<φ* values>       ! phi* [deg]
142	
143	0error detected by nag library routine   d01fce - ifail =     2
144	```
145	
146	Key parameters for η electroproduction (ep → e'pη):
147	
148	| Parameter | Value | Notes |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| `model` | `3` | EtaMAID (maid2000 slot, updated to EtaMAID-2023 tables) |
151	| `ivec` | `1` | Detected recoil proton |
152	| `bmom` | `6.53` | CLAS12 beam momentum [GeV] |
153	| `vcut` | `0.166` | Inelasticity cut [GeV²] used in CLAS12 η analysis |
154	
155	The maximum number of points per file is **10** (Fortran reader limit).
156	For larger grids, use `scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py` which chunks
157	automatically. See `examples/README.md` for annotated input files and
158	`examples/input_multi_chunk.dat` for the multi-row layout used when N > 10.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Generating and running a grid
163	
164	### 1. Generate inputs
165	
166	```bash
167	python3 scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py \
168	  --w-min 1.487 --w-max 1.999 --n-w 30 \
169	  --q2-min 0.3  --q2-max 4.0  --n-q2 30 \
170	  --cos-min -0.9 --cos-max 0.9 --n-cos 30 \
171	  --n-phi 19 \
172	  --tag my_run
173	# Output: rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_<timestamp>/
174	```
175	
176	See `scripts/README.md` for all flags.
177	
178	### 2. Run locally (sequential)
179	
180	```bash
181	./scripts/run_exclurad_grid.sh \
182	  --input-dir rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_...  \
183	  --work-dir  .
184	```
185	
186	For runs near the η threshold or large |cos θ*|, use the unphysical-skip
187	runner instead:
188	
189	```bash
190	./scripts/run_exclurad_skip_unphys.sh \
191	  --input-dir rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_...  \
192	  --work-dir  .                                  \
193	  --timeout-sec 600
194	```
195	
196	### 3. Run on the JLab farm (Slurm)
197	
198	```bash
199	# Build index
200	find rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_... -name '*.dat' | LC_ALL=C sort > inputs.index
201	
202	# Submit array (100 files per task, 50 concurrent)
203	N=$(wc -l < inputs.index)
204	TASKS=$(( (N + 99) / 100 - 1 ))
205	sbatch --array=0-${TASKS}%50 slurm/exclurad_run_chunk.sbatch \
206	  --index-file   $(pwd)/inputs.index                           \
207	  --exe-path     $(pwd)/build/exclurad.exe                     \
208	  --results-root /volatile/clas12/$USER/exclurad/results       \
209	  --count        100
210	```
211	
212	See `slurm/README.md` for the full set of batch scripts and workflows.
213	
214	---
215	
216	## η-channel modifications (2025)
217	
218	The following source-level changes were made relative to the original 2002
219	pion code to support η electroproduction:
220	
221	| File | Change |
222	|---|---|
223	| `exclurad.F` | η mass, beam energy default, output formatting |
224	| `mpintp.inc` | Channel constants, grid dimensions for EtaMAID |
225	| `maid07-PPpi.tbl` | Replaced with EtaMAID-2023 tables (V. Kashevarov) |
226	| `fint.F` | CERNLIB-free replacement for numerical integration |
227	
228	The pion tables (`maid07-NPpi.tbl`, `maid98-PNpi.tbl`, `maid98-PPpi.tbl`)

230	The original pion version remains available at the
231	[JLab RC page](https://www.jlab.org/RC/) and [Exclurad Pion Github Repo](https://github.com/JeffersonLab/exclurad/tree/main).

# EXCLURAD

Fortran code for calculation of QED radiative corrections to exclusive
electroproduction on the nucleon. The current repository contains two
configurations:

- **Pion electroproduction** (original 2002 code): corrections to the
  unpolarized coincidence cross section and beam spin asymmetry (fifth
  structure function) for ep → e'nπ⁺.
- **η-meson electroproduction** (2025 extension): adapted for ep → e'pη
  using updated EtaMAID-2023 hadronic model tables and CLAS12 kinematics.

Distinctive features of the underlying formalism:
- Covariant infrared divergence cancellation (Bardin–Shumeiko method),
  giving results independent of the soft/hard photon splitting parameter.
- Exact integration over the bremsstrahlung photon phase space — no
  peaking approximation.

The code is extendable to any exclusive two-body electroproduction process,
e.g. p(e,e'K)Λ, d(e,e'p)n, ³He(e,e'p)d.

---

## References

Original pion code:

> A. Afanasev, I. Akushevich, V. Burkert, K. Joo,  
> *QED Radiative Corrections in Processes of Exclusive Pion Electroproduction*,  
> Phys. Rev. D **66**, 074004 (2002). [hep-ph/0208183](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0208183)

η-meson extension:

> I. Illari, A. Afanasev, W.J. Briscoe, V.L. Kashevarov, A. Schmidt, I. Strakovsky,  
> *Amplitude-Based Analysis of QED Radiative Corrections to Electroproduction of η-Mesons on Protons*,  
> [arXiv:2604.22943](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22943),
> [accepted in Phys. Rev. D](https://journals.aps.org/prd/accepted/10.1103/78q1-72dn) (2026).

Code and data archived at [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18970109](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18970109).

---

## Interactive RC Explorer

A browser-based visualisation of the η-channel radiative correction output
(δ = σ_obs/σ₀ and A_RC/A_Born) is available at:

**<https://izzyillari.github.io/exclurad/>**

The dataset was computed with the η-channel configuration described below
(vcut = 0.166 GeV², beam energy 6.53 GeV, full O(α) corrections) and now
covers the full production grid: W = 1.487–2.211 GeV, Q² = 0.3–5.0 GeV²,
cos θ* = ±0.9, full φ* range — about 1.9 million kinematic points.
Use the sliders to fix two kinematic variables and plot curves overlaid
by a third.

---

## Repository layout

```
exclurad/
├── exclurad.F          # Main Fortran source (η-modified)
├── fint.F              # CERNLIB-free numerical integration
├── mpintp.inc          # Mass/channel constants (η configuration)
├── spp.inc             # Kinematics include
├── maid07-PPpi.tbl     # EtaMAID-2023 hadronic model table
├── Makefile            # GNU make build
├── sconscript          # SCons build
├── sconstruct          # SCons build
├── input.dat           # Template input file (η defaults, 10 points)
├── examples/           # Annotated example input files
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── input_single_chunk.dat   # 10-point example
│   └── input_multi_chunk.dat    # 50-point multi-row example
├── scripts/            # Input generation and local runners
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── rcgrid_inputgen.py       # 4D kinematic grid generator
│   ├── run_exclurad_grid.sh     # Verbose sequential runner
│   └── run_exclurad_skip_unphys.sh  # Runner with unphysical-skip detection
└── slurm/              # JLab farm batch scripts
    ├── README.md
    ├── exclurad_one_input.sbatch       # Single-file test job
    ├── exclurad_run_chunk.sbatch       # Chunk array (pre-generated grid)
    ├── exclu_30x30_WQ2scan_array.sbatch # Self-contained W×Q² array job
    └── exclu_vcut_scan.sbatch          # ν_cut scan at fixed kinematics
```

---

## Getting started

### Clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JeffersonLab/exclurad.git
cd exclurad
```

### Build

```bash
# GNU make
make

# or SCons (original build system)
scons
```

The executable is written to `build/exclurad.exe`.

On the JLab interactive farm (`ifarm`), GNU Fortran (GCC) 11.5.0 is
available at `/usr/bin/gfortran` with no environment modules required.

### Run a single input

```bash
./build/exclurad.exe < input.dat
```

Outputs are written to the current directory: `all.dat`, `allu.dat`,
`radasm.dat`, `radcor.dat`, `radsigmi.dat`, `radsigpl.dat`, `radtot.dat`.

---

## Input file format

```
3       !  1: AO  2: maid98  3: maid2000
0       !  0: Full, 1: Factorizable and Leading log
6.53    !  bmom - lepton momentum [GeV]
0.0     !  tmom - momentum per nucleon
1       !  lepton - 1 electron, 2 muon
1       !  ivec  - detected hadron (1) p, (2) pi+
0.166   !  vcut  - cut on inelasticity [GeV²] (0 = no cut)

10 ! no. of points
<W values>        ! W [GeV]
<Q² values>       ! Q² [GeV²]
<cos(θ*) values>  ! Cos(Theta*)
<φ* values>       ! phi* [deg]

0error detected by nag library routine   d01fce - ifail =     2
```

Key parameters for η electroproduction (ep → e'pη):

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `3` | EtaMAID (maid2000 slot, updated to EtaMAID-2023 tables) |
| `ivec` | `1` | Detected recoil proton |
| `bmom` | `6.53` | CLAS12 beam momentum [GeV] |
| `vcut` | `0.166` | Inelasticity cut [GeV²] used in CLAS12 η analysis |

The maximum number of points per file is **10** (Fortran reader limit).
For larger grids, use `scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py` which chunks
automatically. See `examples/README.md` for annotated input files and
`examples/input_multi_chunk.dat` for the multi-row layout used when N > 10.

---

## Generating and running a grid

### 1. Generate inputs

```bash
python3 scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py \
  --w-min 1.487 --w-max 1.999 --n-w 30 \
  --q2-min 0.3  --q2-max 4.0  --n-q2 30 \
  --cos-min -0.9 --cos-max 0.9 --n-cos 30 \
  --n-phi 19 \
  --tag my_run
# Output: rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_<timestamp>/
```

See `scripts/README.md` for all flags.

### 2. Run locally (sequential)

```bash
./scripts/run_exclurad_grid.sh \
  --input-dir rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_...  \
  --work-dir  .
```

For runs near the η threshold or large |cos θ*|, use the unphysical-skip
runner instead:

```bash
./scripts/run_exclurad_skip_unphys.sh \
  --input-dir rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_...  \
  --work-dir  .                                  \
  --timeout-sec 600
```

### 3. Run on the JLab farm (Slurm)

```bash
# Build index
find rcgrid-phi_sweep_grid_my_run_... -name '*.dat' | LC_ALL=C sort > inputs.index

# Submit array (100 files per task, 50 concurrent)
N=$(wc -l < inputs.index)
TASKS=$(( (N + 99) / 100 - 1 ))
sbatch --array=0-${TASKS}%50 slurm/exclurad_run_chunk.sbatch \
  --index-file   $(pwd)/inputs.index                           \
  --exe-path     $(pwd)/build/exclurad.exe                     \
  --results-root /volatile/clas12/$USER/exclurad/results       \
  --count        100
```

See `slurm/README.md` for the full set of batch scripts and workflows.

---

## η-channel modifications (2025)

The following source-level changes were made relative to the original 2002
pion code to support η electroproduction:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `exclurad.F` | η mass, beam energy default, output formatting |
| `mpintp.inc` | Channel constants, grid dimensions for EtaMAID |
| `maid07-PPpi.tbl` | Replaced with EtaMAID-2023 tables (V. Kashevarov) |
| `fint.F` | CERNLIB-free replacement for numerical integration |

The pion tables (`maid07-NPpi.tbl`, `maid98-PNpi.tbl`, `maid98-PPpi.tbl`)
are no longer included; this repository targets η production only.
The original pion version remains available at the
[JLab RC page](https://www.jlab.org/RC/) and [Exclurad Pion Github Repo](https://github.com/JeffersonLab/exclurad/tree/main).

1	# examples/
2	
3	Example input files for exclurad, configured for η-meson electroproduction
4	with CLAS12 kinematics.
5	
6	## Input file format
7	
8	```
9	<model>    !  1: AO  2: maid98  3: maid2000
10	<rc_mode>  !  0: Full  1: Factorizable and Leading log
11	<bmom>     !  bmom - lepton momentum [GeV]
12	<tmom>     !  tmom - momentum per nucleon
13	<lepton>   !  lepton - 1 electron, 2 muon
14	<ivec>     !  ivec  - detected hadron (1) p, (2) pi+
15	<vcut>     !  vcut  - cut on inelasticity [GeV^2]
16	
17	<N> ! no. of points
18	<W_1> <W_2> ... <W_N>       ! W values [GeV]
19	<Q2_1> <Q2_2> ... <Q2_N>    ! Q^2 values [GeV^2]
20	<cos_1> <cos_2> ... <cos_N> ! Cos(Theta*) values
21	<phi_1> <phi_2> ... <phi_N> ! phi* values [deg]
22	
23	0error detected by nag library routine   d01fce - ifail =     2
24	```
25	
26	### Parameter notes
27	
28	**model**: Controls the hadronic model used to compute the Born cross section.
29	For η electroproduction, use `3` (maid2000/EtaMAID). Options `1` (AO) and
30	`2` (maid98) are for pion electroproduction.
31	
32	**rc_mode**: `0` computes the full O(α) radiative correction. `1` uses the
33	factorizable leading-log approximation, which is faster but less accurate.
34	
35	**bmom**: Beam lepton momentum in GeV. For CLAS12 running at 6.535 GeV,
36	use `6.53`.
37	
38	**ivec**: The detected recoil hadron. For η electroproduction (ep → e'pη),
39	the recoil proton is detected: use `1`. For pion electroproduction
40	(ep → e'nπ+), use `2`.
41	
42	**vcut**: Inelasticity cut in GeV². Setting `vcut = 0.166` corresponds to
43	the cut used in the CLAS12 η analysis. Set to `0` to apply no cut. A
44	negative value sets a cut on v directly rather than on v² — see the EXCLURAD
45	paper (Afanasev et al., Phys. Rev. D 66, 2002) for definitions.
46	
47	**N and data lines**: All four kinematic arrays must have exactly N entries.
48	N is limited to 10 per file by the Fortran reader. For larger grids, use
49	`scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py`, which chunks automatically.
50	
51	The trailing `0error...` line is a legacy artifact from the original NAG
52	library integration routine. It must be present for the parser to terminate
53	correctly.
54	
55	### Multi-row layout (N > 10)
56	
57	For N > 10, values can wrap across multiple rows — the Fortran reader is
58	whitespace-delimited and ignores line breaks within a data block. The `!`
59	comment marker on the last row of each block is the only required annotation.
60	See `input_multi_chunk.dat` for an example with N = 50.
61	
62	---
63	
64	## Files
65	
66	### input_single_chunk.dat
67	
68	A single 10-point file. W and Q² are held constant; cos(θ*) varies across
69	10 uniformly spaced values in [−0.28, +0.28]; φ* is fixed at 228°.
70	
71	```
72	W   = 1.540 GeV
73	Q²  = 0.683 GeV²
74	φ*  = 228°
75	cos = −0.279 … +0.279  (10 points)
76	```
77	
78	Run directly:
79	```bash
80	./build/exclurad.exe < examples/input_single_chunk.dat
81	```
82	
83	### input_multi_chunk.dat
84	
85	A 50-point file illustrating the multi-row layout. W and Q² are held
86	constant; cos(θ*) spans the full range [−0.999, +0.999] in 50 uniformly
87	spaced steps; φ* is fixed at 315°.
88	
89	```
90	W   = 1.675 GeV
91	Q²  = 1.253 GeV²
92	φ*  = 315°
93	cos = −0.999 … +0.999  (50 points)
94	```
95	
96	Run directly:
97	```bash
98	./build/exclurad.exe < examples/input_multi_chunk.dat
99	```
100	
101	Note: despite N = 50, this is a single call to the executable — the Fortran
102	reader parses multi-row blocks correctly. The ≤10-per-file limit only applies
103	when using the batch runner scripts, which stage `input.dat` one file at a
104	time.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Generating your own inputs
109	
110	For production grids, use `scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py` rather than writing
111	input files by hand. It generates a full 4D grid in W, Q², cos(θ*), and φ*,
112	handles chunking automatically, and produces a `manifest.csv` for tracking.
113	
114	```bash
115	python3 scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py --help
116	```
117	
118	See `scripts/README.md` for a full walkthrough.
119

<bmom>     !  bmom - lepton momentum [GeV]
<tmom>     !  tmom - momentum per nucleon

<ivec>     !  ivec  - detected hadron (1) p, (2) pi+
<vcut>     !  vcut  - cut on inelasticity [GeV^2]

<N> ! no. of points
<W_1> <W_2> ... <W_N>       ! W values [GeV]
<Q2_1> <Q2_2> ... <Q2_N>    ! Q^2 values [GeV^2]
<cos_1> <cos_2> ... <cos_N> ! Cos(Theta*) values
<phi_1> <phi_2> ... <phi_N> ! phi* values [deg]

0error detected by nag library routine   d01fce - ifail =     2
```

### Parameter notes

**model**: Controls the hadronic model used to compute the Born cross section.
For η electroproduction, use `3` (maid2000/EtaMAID). Options `1` (AO) and
`2` (maid98) are for pion electroproduction.

**rc_mode**: `0` computes the full O(α) radiative correction. `1` uses the
factorizable leading-log approximation, which is faster but less accurate.

**bmom**: Beam lepton momentum in GeV. For CLAS12 running at 6.535 GeV,
use `6.53`.

**ivec**: The detected recoil hadron. For η electroproduction (ep → e'pη),
the recoil proton is detected: use `1`. For pion electroproduction
(ep → e'nπ+), use `2`.

**vcut**: Inelasticity cut in GeV². Setting `vcut = 0.166` corresponds to
the cut used in the CLAS12 η analysis. Set to `0` to apply no cut. A
negative value sets a cut on v directly rather than on v² — see the EXCLURAD
paper (Afanasev et al., Phys. Rev. D 66, 2002) for definitions.

**N and data lines**: All four kinematic arrays must have exactly N entries.
N is limited to 10 per file by the Fortran reader. For larger grids, use
`scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py`, which chunks automatically.

The trailing `0error...` line is a legacy artifact from the original NAG
library integration routine. It must be present for the parser to terminate
correctly.

### Multi-row layout (N > 10)

For N > 10, values can wrap across multiple rows — the Fortran reader is
whitespace-delimited and ignores line breaks within a data block. The `!`
comment marker on the last row of each block is the only required annotation.
See `input_multi_chunk.dat` for an example with N = 50.

---

## Files

### input_single_chunk.dat

A single 10-point file. W and Q² are held constant; cos(θ*) varies across
10 uniformly spaced values in [−0.28, +0.28]; φ* is fixed at 228°.

```
W   = 1.540 GeV
Q²  = 0.683 GeV²
φ*  = 228°
cos = −0.279 … +0.279  (10 points)
```

Run directly:
```bash
./build/exclurad.exe < examples/input_single_chunk.dat
```

### input_multi_chunk.dat

A 50-point file illustrating the multi-row layout. W and Q² are held
constant; cos(θ*) spans the full range [−0.999, +0.999] in 50 uniformly
spaced steps; φ* is fixed at 315°.

```
W   = 1.675 GeV
Q²  = 1.253 GeV²
φ*  = 315°
cos = −0.999 … +0.999  (50 points)
```

Run directly:
```bash
./build/exclurad.exe < examples/input_multi_chunk.dat
```

Note: despite N = 50, this is a single call to the executable — the Fortran
reader parses multi-row blocks correctly. The ≤10-per-file limit only applies
when using the batch runner scripts, which stage `input.dat` one file at a
time.

---

## Generating your own inputs

For production grids, use `scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py` rather than writing
input files by hand. It generates a full 4D grid in W, Q², cos(θ*), and φ*,
handles chunking automatically, and produces a `manifest.csv` for tracking.

```bash
python3 scripts/rcgrid_inputgen.py --help
```

See `scripts/README.md` for a full walkthrough.
